title: She didn’t wait for the silence… she sang while the water was still roaring.
paragraphs: She didn’t wait for the silence… she sang while the water was still roaring.
Let that hit you.

Not when everything made sense.
Not when the future was clear.
Not when the fear was gone.
While it was still messy… Miriam lifted her tambourine. (Exodus 15:20–21)

The sea had just swallowed an army.
Chariots crushed. Horses gone. The terror of Egypt erased in a moment.
But don’t romanticize it too quickly.

Their clothes were still wet.
Their hearts were still racing.
Their future? Completely unknown.

Behind them—death defeated.
Before them—a wilderness with no guarantees.
And right there, in the tension between miracle and uncertainty…
She chose to sing.
Let me ask you something, kapatid:

What kind of person praises God
before life stabilizes?
Because most of us don’t.

We worship when the bills are paid.
We post testimonies when the prayers are answered.
We lift our hands when the outcome is already secured.
But Miriam?

She turned her breakthrough into a soundtrack of faith—
before she saw provision, before she saw direction, before she saw tomorrow.
Here’s the scandal:
Her praise wasn’t based on what might happen.
It was rooted in what God had already done.
“Sing to the LORD, for He has triumphed gloriously…” (Exodus 15:21)

She wasn’t guessing.
She was remembering.

And remembrance became rhythm.
Rhythm became worship.
Worship became warfare against fear.
Because let’s be honest…
Some of you are standing exactly where Miriam stood.
You just survived something that should’ve destroyed you.

A breakup.
A betrayal.
A hidden battle no one clapped for.
God brought you through—but now?
You’re staring at a season that makes no sense.

No clear next step.
No visible provision.
No emotional closure.
Just… space.
And in that space, fear whispers:
“Stay quiet. Don’t celebrate yet. What if it all falls apart again?”

But hear me—
that voice is not from the Shepherd.

Because the same God who split the sea
did not lose His power overnight.
He didn’t bring you this far to abandon you in the unknown.
Miriam understood something many of us forget:
Praise is not a reaction. It’s a declaration.
It declares:

God is still good—
even when I don’t understand.

God is still faithful—
even when I can’t trace Him.

God is still working—
even when I can’t see results yet.
And here’s where the story deepens.

Because Miriam’s song was powerful…
but it was still pointing forward to a greater victory.
A better Exodus.
Centuries later, another moment came that looked like defeat.

No parted sea.
No tambourines.
No dancing crowds.
Just a cross.
Blood. Nails. Silence.
And if you were there that day, you wouldn’t have sung.
You would have wept.
Because it looked like evil had won.
But three days later—
Jesus walked out of the grave. (Matthew 28:6)

Not symbolic.
Not poetic.
Literal. Bodily. Victorious.
And in that moment, the greatest enemy wasn’t Pharaoh.

It was sin.
It was death.
It was the weight of our guilt—and Christ crushed it completely.
So now we don’t just sing because of a sea that opened.
We sing because of a tomb that couldn’t stay closed.
Listen carefully:
Miriam sang after a temporary deliverance.
We sing because of an eternal one.
Her victory led to a wilderness.
Our victory leads to redemption, restoration, and a promised future in Christ.
So why are you still holding your praise hostage?

Waiting for clarity.
Waiting for control.
Waiting for everything to “feel right.”
God is not asking for perfect conditions.
He’s asking for a surrendered heart that trusts Him anyway.
Maybe today your song sounds weak.

Maybe it trembles.
Maybe it breaks in the middle.
Sing anyway.

Because faith is not the absence of fear—
it’s the decision to trust God in the presence of it.
Lift your “tambourine.”

Your voice.
Your prayer.
Your quiet surrender.
Not because everything is fixed…
But because Jesus already finished the most important battle.

If He conquered sin—
He can handle your situation.

If He defeated death—
He can carry your future.

If He rose again—
then your story is not over.
So today, don’t wait for the waters to settle.
Sing while they’re still moving.

Someone is standing at their Red Sea right now—
and they need a reason to open their mouth again.
